tasks.short: Write and check specifications for our HR dashboards, AFAS extracts and reporting changes.

today.trigger: Assumed current workflow: HR requests a new report, a metric changes, or an AFAS change affects an existing dashboard.
steps: Clarify the question, audience and metric definition with the HR requester.
Inspect the nightly AFAS extract, Power BI model and existing specifications in SharePoint.
Document source fields, joins, calculations, refresh timing and access rules.
Check examples against AFAS totals and investigate differences.
Review the specification with the metric owner and save the approved version in SharePoint.
drudgery: Copying field names and relationships into documents.
Comparing old specifications with the current reporting model.
Repeating the same refresh, access and validation sections.
Finding which definition or document version was approved.
today.time_sinks: Reconciling source fields with business definitions, documenting exceptions across sites and CAOs, and chasing decisions about ambiguous metrics.

lenses.faster: Extract fields, relationships and calculations from the reporting model and generate the first specification from a standard template. Manual copying and document comparison largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A reporting-model change triggers a draft specification, a change summary and validation results. The analyst receives an approval request only after the automated checks finish.
lenses.ambitious: Keep a current specification and a small set of reconciliation checks for every important HR metric. Give the 90-day productive-and-retained measure explicit cohort, productivity and retention definitions.
lenses.joy: Remove transcription and version checking so the analyst can spend more time resolving unclear business questions. Reviewing a concrete discrepancy is more useful than maintaining boilerplate.
lenses.options: Show alternative definitions where the business meaning is unsettled, such as calendar days versus working days for time to hire. Compare the effect of each definition on a sample before choosing one.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the reporting specification standard, metric dictionary and quality checks. They improve the documentation process instead of writing each specification from scratch.
reach: Maintain the Controller's shared definitions for headcount, FTE and labour cost.
Prepare technical reporting handovers for HR Administrators and the Payroll Specialist.
Document recruitment and learning-data interfaces with Recruitee and Studytube.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst resolves what a metric should mean, checks whether CAO and site differences are represented correctly, and challenges misleading conclusions. The responsible HR or Finance owner approves business definitions.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic software extracts metadata and runs reconciliations; an llm_step turns approved requirements and metadata into readable documentation. A human gate remains necessary because technically consistent calculations can still represent the wrong business definition.

in_practice.trigger: An approved reporting-change request or a detected change to the reporting model starts the workflow.
steps: Read the changed model metadata, approved requirement and existing specification using read-only access.
Compare fields, joins, calculations and access rules with the previous version.
Run defined schema and reconciliation checks against an approved test extract.
Generate a draft specification with source references, test results and unresolved questions.
Route the draft to the analyst and metric owner; publish the approved version and retain its change history.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves technical accuracy and access rules; the metric owner approves new or changed business definitions before the specification becomes authoritative. Production reporting changes require their own release approval.
data_needed: Reporting model fields, relationships and calculations.
Approved metric definitions and specification template.
Relevant AFAS field mappings and permitted CAO distinctions.
Aggregated reconciliation totals or synthetic test records.
Report access matrix and designated metric owners.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint reporting-change register containing model version, source references, check results, draft location and named approvals; exclude raw employee records.

evidence.claim: Power BI Desktop exposes model tables, relationships and calculations that can support technical specifications.
SharePoint document libraries support version history for specifications and approved revisions.
An LLM can draft readable specifications from supplied metadata and requirements, but business meaning needs review.
A 65% reduction in hands-on work and a 2.2-times end-to-end speedup are planning estimates for this proposed workflow, not measured Noordhaven results.

risks: Generated documentation can faithfully describe an incorrect calculation; reconciliation and business-definition approval must both pass.
Missing history for site transfers, contracts or agency workers can distort headcount and 90-day cohorts.
Employee-level payroll and absence data can enter prompts or logs unnecessarily; use metadata, synthetic records and aggregated checks wherever possible.
Access to documentation can reveal sensitive fields or reporting permissions, so the specification library needs appropriate restrictions.
Extending this workflow into employee monitoring may require works council consent under the WOR and an AVG/GDPR assessment.
research_questions: Can the current Power BI deployment expose model metadata and changes through supported read-only access?
What share of the 51.5 annual hours is transcription and comparison versus resolving business definitions?
Are approved definitions and reliable reconciliation totals available for headcount, absence and the 90-day hire measure?
Does a pilot on three reporting changes reduce total drafting, correction and review effort without introducing material specification errors?

tasks.short: Track HR technology changes and recommend improvements to hiring, onboarding, reporting and workforce administration.

today.trigger: Assumed company interpretation of the O*NET task: an HR technology review, vendor release or recurring process problem prompts research.
steps: Gather release notes, vendor information and relevant Dutch regulatory updates.
Check which changes apply to AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft 365.
Compare capabilities with Noordhaven's hiring, onboarding and reporting problems.
Estimate integration effort, costs and privacy or works council implications.
Write a recommendation and discuss priorities with the HR Director and affected specialists.
drudgery: Checking several vendor websites for changes.
Copying feature descriptions into comparison spreadsheets.
Rechecking whether a feature is released, licensed and available in the Dutch environment.
today.time_sinks: Separating useful capabilities from sales claims and establishing whether a change actually fits Noordhaven's licences, interfaces, shift workers and Dutch obligations.

lenses.faster: Collect changes from a fixed source list, remove duplicates and draft a comparison with links to the original material. The analyst checks shortlisted changes instead of reading every announcement.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled scan creates an internal digest and flags changes that match recorded HR problems. Buying software, starting trials and changing employee processes remain human decisions.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a continuous improvement backlog tied to productive hires retained after 90 days. Evaluate small changes such as clearer onboarding handoffs before considering a major system replacement.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive searching and marketing summaries. Keep conversations with warehouse managers, hands-on trials and the judgment about what will help people on shifts.
lenses.options: For each problem, compare configuring an existing system, building a small integration, buying a tool, changing the process and leaving it unchanged. Show costs, dependencies and expected effects using the same assumptions.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the technology watchlist, evidence standard and trial scorecard. Their work becomes choosing and validating improvements across the HR system landscape.
reach: Prepare evidence briefs for the HR Director's technology priorities.
Help Recruiters and L&D Specialists assess features in Recruitee and Studytube.
Prepare integration and licence-cost assumptions for the Controller and FP&A Analysts.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges fit with actual warehouse work, challenges vendor evidence and tests whether an improvement affects the North Star. HR leadership, IT and affected process owners retain decisions about investment and employee impact.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow collects changing external information, interprets relevance and handles unavailable or conflicting sources. It can publish a clearly labelled internal digest automatically, but recommendations that lead to spending or employee-process changes need human approval.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly schedule or a new entry in the approved HR improvement backlog starts a scan.
steps: Fetch accessible material from approved vendor and official regulatory sources, recording publication dates and links.
Extract changes, availability, licence conditions and stated integration requirements; mark missing details as unknown.
Match changes to Noordhaven's system inventory, process problems and agreed evaluation criteria.
Publish a source-linked internal digest and draft option comparisons for relevant changes.
Have the analyst validate shortlisted claims and route any proposed trial or purchase to the responsible owners.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine internal digests need exception review rather than approval each time. The analyst verifies material claims before presenting a recommendation; HR, IT and procurement approve trials or purchases, with privacy and OR involvement where required.
systems: Official Dutch and EU regulatory sources
SharePoint technology inventory and improvement backlog
data_needed: Current systems, versions, licences and supported interfaces.
Approved source list and previous scan results.
HR process problems, owners and priorities.
Aggregated hiring, onboarding, retention and absence baselines.
Privacy, security and works council requirements relevant to each proposed use.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint technology-watch register containing source links, retrieval dates, extracted claims, unknowns, relevance reasons and subsequent human decisions.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, duplicate removal and comparisons against a fixed system inventory can reduce repeated research work.
An LLM can turn supplied release notes into a structured comparison, provided the workflow preserves sources and checks important claims.
Technology adoption decisions still require local evidence about integration, licensing and effects on work.
A 55% reduction in hands-on work and a 1.8-times end-to-end speedup are planning estimates; Noordhaven's collection coverage and review effort are untested.

risks: Vendor claims may describe roadmap features, additional licences or capabilities unavailable in Noordhaven's environment.
Automated ranking can favour frequent announcements over improvements that matter to shift workers or managers.
External pages can contain misleading content or instructions; treat them as research data and give the collection workflow no purchasing or system-change permissions.

Tools used for recruitment selection or worker-management decisions may fall under EU AI Act high-risk rules; assess the intended use before a trial. A general technology digest is not automatically high-risk.
Personnel-data processing or monitoring changes may require OR consent under the WOR, an AVG/GDPR assessment and possibly a DPIA.
Absence-related proposals must respect Wet verbetering poortwachter responsibilities and the separation of medical information held by the bedrijfsarts.
research_questions: Which relevant release notes are accessible automatically, and which require manual portal access or vendor confirmation?
What share of the 44.7 annual hours is collection and summarising versus stakeholder discussion and evaluation?
Can a six-week pilot find useful changes while keeping false positives and claim-checking effort low?
Can shortlisted improvements be tested against week-one onboarding or 90-day retention without using individual employee scores or introducing unapproved monitoring?

role.altitude: The role becomes the owner of trustworthy HR measures and the improvement process for Noordhaven's connected HR systems. The analyst sets definitions, tests data quality and validates whether system changes improve hiring through day 90.
reach: Own shared headcount, FTE and labour-cost definitions with Finance.
Coordinate data-quality checks across AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube.
Prepare recruitment-funnel and onboarding analyses for Recruiters and HR Business Partners.
Prepare certificate-completion and expiry reporting for L&D, subject to reliable source data.
Prepare evidence and cost assumptions for HR technology decisions.
role.ceiling_note: These two tasks total 96.2 hours annually, about 6% of the role. The proposed hands-on savings total approximately 58 hours a year, worth about EUR 4,530 of capacity at EUR 78/hour; they are not cash savings or evidence that the whole role can be automated. Speedups describe elapsed task time and are lower than the hands-on reductions because review and coordination remain. Wider gains depend on interfaces, data history, agreed definitions and adoption by process owners; the analyst does not take over payroll sign-off, medical judgments or employment decisions.
skills_to_grow: SQL and data modelling for consistent cohorts across employees, sites and staffing agencies.
Power BI model metadata, version control and automated reconciliation.
Writing testable metric definitions and clear acceptance criteria.
Evaluating generated text against source evidence and handling unsupported claims.
AVG/GDPR, works council involvement and EU AI Act assessment for HR use cases.
Designing small trials and distinguishing correlation from evidence of improvement.
role.ambitious_version: Build a joined-up view from vacancy to day 90 using Recruitee hiring events, AFAS employment history and Studytube onboarding records where lawful and technically feasible. Agree a practical productivity definition with site managers, publish reliable cohort measures, and run small process trials that show which changes improve productive hires retained after 90 days.
